from harvests import feed_harvests, ROWS
from halves import split_window

VALUES = [v for _, v in ROWS]


def test_second_half():
    first, second = split_window(feed_harvests(), 4)
    assert second == VALUES[2:4]


def test_first_half():
    first, second = split_window(feed_harvests(), 4)
    assert first == VALUES[:2]


def test_odd_size():
    first, second = split_window(feed_harvests(), 3)
    assert first == VALUES[:1] and second == VALUES[1:3]


def test_reads_only_the_window():
    feed = feed_harvests()
    split_window(feed, 2)
    assert next(feed).kilos == ROWS[2][1]

def split_window(feed, size):
    """Read the next `size` harvests from the feed and return their kilos as (first half, second half).

    The feed may be endless. Exactly `size` items are read from it.
    """
    window = [x.kilos for x in itertools.islice(feed, size)]
    half = size // 2
    return window[:half], window[half:]
